accounts.provider: Which messenger the account belongs to, as a lowercase name such as `telegram` or `max`; open-ended so new adapters need no change.
accounts.name: The account's display name as the messenger reports it; NULL when not known.

sync_cursors.key: Name of what a sync remembers for this account, e.g. `chat_list_complete`, `history_start:<chatId>`, `fetched:<chatId>`, or a provider delta marker.
sync_cursors.value: The remembered value as text (a delta marker, a message id, a JSON list); callers encode numbers themselves.

sync_ranges.from_key: Lowest provider ordering key (Telegram's message id) of a stretch of the chat held completely; missing messages inside it were deleted.
sync_ranges.to_key: Highest provider ordering key of that complete stretch; messages outside every stretch were simply never fetched.

fetch_leases.anchor: Which stretch or job of the chat is being fetched, as a label such as `gaps`, so two processes never fetch the same pages.
fetch_leases.holder: Random id (a UUID) of the process that currently holds the lease.
fetch_leases.expires_at: When the lease runs out (epoch ms); after it another holder may take the stretch.

persons.name: Display name of the person (taken from their first identity's name); NULL if none known.
persons.owner: 1 for the person who owns the store; a new store creates that row, so it always exists.

identities.provider: Messenger the identity lives in (`telegram`, `max`, or any string such as `email`); one identity per provider, not per account.
identities.username: The person's public handle in that messenger, without `@`; NULL when they have none.
identities.name: The person's current display name as the messenger last reported it.
identities.bot: 1 if the messenger says this identity is a bot, 0 if it says not, NULL when unknown.
identities.phone_hmac: Keyed hash (HMAC) of the person's phone number, for matching the same person across messengers; the number itself never reaches a log, fixture or document. No tool fills it yet.

identity_links.method: How the identity was assigned to its person: `initial` when first seen, or a caller's label such as `manual` or `same-email`.
identity_links.confidence: How sure the link is, from 0 to 1; 1 for every link the store writes.
identity_links.author: Who decided the link: `ingest` for the automatic first link, otherwise `owner` or the name of a program.

identity_link_events.method: How this move of an identity between persons was decided (`initial`, `manual`, `same-email`…), kept so a bad link can be undone.
identity_link_events.author: Who made this move: `ingest`, `owner`, or a program's name.

identity_revisions.name: The display name the person had at this snapshot of their profile (a row is added only when the profile changes).
identity_revisions.username: The handle (without `@`) the person had at this snapshot.
identity_revisions.description: The person's self-written bio/about text at this snapshot.

entities.kind: Type of the owner-defined thing: one of `organization`, `family`, `project`, `group`.
entities.name: The entity's name as the owner gave it.

chats.title: The chat's name as the messenger shows it; NULL when it has none.
chats.unread_count: Unread messages the messenger reported; NULL means the messenger did not say, which is not zero.
chats.last_message_at: Time of the chat's newest message (epoch ms); NULL when it never had one.
chats.participants_count: Member count the messenger reported; NULL when not given.
chats.username: The chat's public handle (without `@`) where it has one, e.g. a public channel.
chats.searchable: 1 if the chat's messages appear in searches that do not name it, 0 if only a search naming the chat sees them.

member_stays.first_seen_at: When a member-list read first showed the person in the group for this stay (epoch ms).
member_stays.last_seen_at: When a member-list read last showed the person in the group (epoch ms).
member_stays.role: The person's role in the group at the last read: `owner`, `admin` or `member`; NULL when not given.
member_stays.left_at: When a complete member list first lacked the person, closing this stay (epoch ms); NULL while they are still in it.

messages.thread_external_id: The messenger's id of the topic or thread inside the chat the message belongs to, where the messenger has threads.
messages.sender_chat_external_id: The messenger's id of the chat that authored the message (a channel post or a message sent as the group); NULL for a person.
messages.sender_name: The sender's display name as carried on this message.
messages.sent_at: When the message was sent (epoch ms).
messages.edited_at: When the messenger last recorded an edit (epoch ms); NULL for a message never changed.
messages.text: The message text exactly as received (empty string when there is none or it was deleted).
messages.reply_to_external_id: The messenger's id of the message this one replies to, even when no copy of it was sent.
messages.reply_to: JSON copy of the replied-to message as the messenger sent it (id, sender, time, text, attachments); NULL when not sent.
messages.forward: JSON copy of the original message this one forwards (same shape as reply_to); NULL when not a forward.
messages.outgoing: 1 if this account sent it, 0 if someone else did, NULL when the account's own identity is unknown.
messages.reactions: JSON of the reactions: counts per reaction, this account's own reaction and the total; NULL when never asked.
messages.source: How the message reached the store, e.g. `history`, `send`, `backfill`, `update`, `context`; diagnostic only.
messages.normalizer_version: Version of the text-normalisation rules that produced the message's search text (currently 1); NULL until normalised.

message_revisions.text: The message text before an edit replaced it.
message_revisions.edited_at: The edit time (epoch ms) the message carried while it had this older text; NULL if it was not edited before.

message_links.source: Who proposed this parent for the message: `provider` (the messenger's own reply), `rule`, or `agent`.
message_links.kind: Why the message is linked to its parent: `reply`, `mention`, `same_sender` (rules/provider) or `answer` (an agent's choice).
message_links.confidence: How sure the source is that this is the right parent, from 0 to 1.
message_links.version: For provider and rule links, the linking-rules version that wrote it (as text); for agent links, the agent's skill version, if given.

message_counter_observations.value: The counter's value at the observation (a non-negative number).
message_counter_observations.source: How it was observed: `remote_fetch` (the store asked) or `remote_update` (the messenger pushed a change).

message_transcripts.message_external_id: The messenger's id of the voice message transcribed; keyed this way because a message can be heard before it is stored.
message_transcripts.text: What the voice message said, as transcribed; never empty.
message_transcripts.heard_at: When the transcript was made (epoch ms).

attachments.kind: Lowercase type of the attachment, such as `photo`, `video`, `file`, `voice`, `sticker`, `share`.
attachments.mime: The file's MIME type, where the messenger gives one.
attachments.name: The file name, where the messenger gives one.
attachments.title: Title of a shared web page (for `share` attachments).
attachments.url: A link that opens the bytes or the shared page, when the messenger hands one out.
attachments.size: File size in bytes, where the messenger gives it.
attachments.width: Width in pixels for images and video.
attachments.height: Height in pixels for images and video.
attachments.duration: Length in seconds for audio and video.
attachments.provider_ref: Opaque JSON the messenger adapter needs to fetch the bytes later; meaningless outside that adapter.
attachments.local_path: Where `messages download` saved the file on this computer; NULL when it was never downloaded.
attachments.extractor: What produced the attachment's text: `plain`, `docx:mammoth@1.13.0`, `pdf:unpdf@1.8.1`, an OCR engine, or an agent's own label.
attachments.extraction_error: Short reason code why no text came out (e.g. `no_text`), never a line of the file; NULL on success.
attachments.content_sha256: Hex SHA-256 of the file bytes that were read, so an unchanged file is not read again.
attachments.extracted_at: When the attachment's text (or its error) was written (epoch ms).

reminders.due_at: When the reminder should fire (epoch ms).
reminders.timezone: IANA time zone the reminder was scheduled in, e.g. `Europe/Madrid`.
reminders.state: Delivery state: `pending`, `leased` (claimed by a deliverer), `delivered` or `cancelled`.
reminders.lease_until: Until when the current deliverer holds the reminder (epoch ms); after it another may claim it. NULL unless leased.
reminders.receipt: Id handed to the deliverer at claim time, which it must return to confirm delivery; NULL when not leased.

links.kind: Type of connection: `links-to` (a note links to something), `about`, `member-of`, `related-to` or `assigned-to`.
links.anchor: The heading or block fragment the link points at inside its target, like `#Heading` or `#^block`; NULL for the whole target.
links.source: Where the link came from: `file` (written in a note file), `owner` (added by the owner) or `suggested` (proposed, not yet confirmed).
links.target_text: The target as written (e.g. a name in a note), kept while the link resolves to nobody; up to 500 characters.
links.target_folded: target_text case- and accent-folded with any leading `@` removed, matched against new person names and aliases to resolve the link.
links.role: The role the relation states, such as a job title in a `member-of` link; free text up to 200 characters.
links.evidence: Free text saying why the relation holds (up to 2000 characters).
links.confirmed: 1 if the owner stands behind the link, 0 if it is only a weak, unconfirmed proposal.

auto_tag_claims.algorithm: Name and version of the rules that assigned the automatic tag, currently `keywords-v1`.
auto_tag_claims.score: Share of the chat's metadata fields (title, username, description) that matched the tag's keywords: 1/3, 2/3 or 1; not a probability.
auto_tag_claims.fields: JSON list of which metadata fields matched, from `title`, `username`, `description`.

searches.name: The saved search's unique name; NULL for an unnamed run kept only as history.
searches.version: Version of the search query language used (currently 1).
searches.fields_version: Version of the list of searchable field names the query was written against (currently 2).
searches.last_run_at: When the search was last run (epoch ms); NULL for a saved search never run.
searches.runs: How many times this search has been run.

conversations.first_at: Send time of the conversation's first message (epoch ms).
conversations.last_at: Send time of the conversation's last message (epoch ms).
conversations.message_count: How many messages the conversation holds.
conversations.built_at: When the build that produced this conversation ran (epoch ms).
conversations.algorithm_version: Version of the linking rules that grouped the messages (currently 5).

conversation_state.enabled_at: When the owner turned on conversation grouping for this chat (epoch ms).
conversation_state.built_at: When the current conversations of this chat were built (epoch ms); NULL before the first build.
conversation_state.algorithm_version: Linking-rules version of the current build; NULL before the first build.

conversation_chunks.ordinal: Position of this chunk within its conversation, from 0.
conversation_chunks.text_end: For a piece of one long message, the offset in that message's text where the piece ends; NULL when the chunk is whole messages.

chunk_vectors.content_hash: Hex SHA-256 of the chunk text the embedding model was given; the text itself is never stored.
chunk_vectors.dims: Number of dimensions in the vector (its float32 length).

search_index_state.watermark: The highest message `pk` when the index was created; rows above it are indexed by triggers, rows up to it by batch fill.
search_index_state.filled_through: The highest message `pk` the batch fill has indexed so far; the index is complete once it reaches the watermark.
search_index_state.terms_through: The highest message `pk` whose words are in the typo-correction vocabulary; 0 means the vocabulary is not built.
search_index_state.normalizer_version: Version of the text-normalisation rules the index was built with.
search_index_state.built_at: When the index finished filling (epoch ms); NULL while it is still being filled.

search_terms.length: Number of characters in the word, used to find typo candidates of a similar length.

search_term_trigrams.trigram: A three-character piece of a known word, used to find words that look like a mistyped one.
search_term_trigrams.length: Character length of the word the trigram comes from.
search_term_trigrams.term: The known search word the trigram belongs to (numbers get no trigrams).

schema_migrations.min_compatible: The oldest schema version whose code can still safely write a file at this version; a build older than it refuses the file.
schema_migrations.applied_at: When this migration was applied to the file (epoch ms).

store_settings.value: The setting's value as text, shared by every profile and messenger using this store file.
store_settings.at: When the setting was last written (epoch ms).

aliases.name: The owner's private name for this contact in this account (1–200 characters); NULL when cleared.
aliases.name_folded: The alias lowercased, used for case-insensitive contact search and for matching names written in notes.
